channel.title: Paperraft
channel.description: Research in efficient inference and AI agents, ranked by independent GitHub implementations instead of citations or stars. Papers above the attention threshold are deliberately excluded.

item.title: Not All Branches Are Equal: Adaptive Semantic ID Construction for Generative Recommendation
item.description: AST replaces fixed-codebook residual or hierarchical vector quantization (e.g., RQ-VAE) for semantic ID construction with a top-down divisive clustering tree whose branching factor is chosen per node by maximizing the silhouette coefficient, plus constrained variants enforcing minimum probability mass for long-tail items. Cost is limited to an offline clustering pass over item embeddings and retraining the generative recommender on the new IDs, which fits a single 24 GB GPU; no serving-time overhead is added. Failure modes include dependence on the quality of the input item embeddings, sensitivity of silhouette-based splitting to dataset density structure, and unverified benefit outside Amazon Review-style domains given the absence of quantified results in the abstract. 0 independent implementations, 31 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: test.

item.title: UTOPI: Efficient Egocentric Long-Video Understanding in AR via User-Guided Token Pre-Compression
item.description: The method replaces uniform frame/token ingestion for egocentric long video with a pre-compression stage that prunes temporally redundant frames using user motion signals and retains foreground tokens guided by eye-tracking fixations. Its cost is a plug-in preprocessing module plus a fine-tuned adjustment network, and it requires AR hardware that exposes motion and gaze streams. It can fail when motion or gaze signals are noisy or unavailable, when user attention diverges from task-relevant content, or in non-egocentric video settings where the redundancy assumptions do not hold. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Perturbing Inputs Improves Pretraining Distillation
item.description: The method replaces standard knowledge distillation during an early phase of pretraining by training the student to match the teacher on perturbed inputs (additive token noise, blended documents, or blended tokens) before reverting to ordinary distillation for the remaining token budget. It costs additional teacher forward passes on perturbed sequences and requires access to both teacher logits and pretraining compute from scratch. The gains can fail to transfer if the reader lacks pretraining infrastructure, relies on third-party APIs that do not expose logits, or operates at scales or data regimes where the reported small-margin improvements vanish. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: distillation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Language model capabilities fail in a shared, predictable order under compression and perturbation
item.description: This is a diagnostic methodology rather than a compression technique: it replaces the assumption that pruning or quantization degrades all capabilities uniformly by measuring per-task fragility under cheap random perturbations and using it to forecast which short-answer capabilities a compressed model will lose first. It costs a perturbation-based evaluation pass plus four-task calibration per deployment, with no extra inference latency or memory in the deployed model. It can fail when profiles are transferred across quantization methods such as GPTQ, when tasks are long-form rather than short-answer, and when the production task distribution differs from the calibrated set. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Why Kubernetes Cannot Contain a Full Lazy-Pulling Cache: Two Impossibility Results and a Bounded, Honest Design for Model Serving
item.description: The method replaces the unbounded, unaccounted node-level cache created by lazy container-image pulling (stargz-snapshotter, SOCI, Nydus) with a cache that enforces a hard byte budget keyed to filesystem truth and pass-through semantics in which a failed cache write never becomes a failed read. It costs approximately 18.5% additional completion time, requires deploying a modified snapshotter component inside the serving nodes, and adds lossy, non-blocking accounting machinery to maintain. It can fail if the workload does not actually use lazy pulling, if the lossy accounting's dropped updates misalign with real pressure in untested conditions, or if the upstream proposal is not merged and the team must maintain a fork. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: serving and batching. Recommendation: test.

item.title: BridgeKV: Large-Model Prefill and Small-Model Decoding for LLM Inference via KV Cache Translation
item.description: The method replaces running the same large model for both prefill and decoding: the large model computes the prompt cache once, a trained stitching module translates that cache into the small model's layout, and the small model decodes all tokens. It costs an offline training stage for the translator (plus optional low-rank adapters), a residual quality gap since only up to 80% of the large-model advantage is recovered, and extra engineering to run two models and transfer caches between phases. It can fail when no same-family model pair exists for the target model, when the translator does not generalize to new domains or long prompts outside its training distribution, and when memory constraints force the prefill model to be offloaded, erasing the latency benefit. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Planners Exploit Deterministic Error: Dithered Low-Bit World Models
item.description: The method replaces round-to-nearest activation quantization in low-bit world models used by sampling-based planners with stochastic rounding whose dither is shared across candidates and redrawn each planner iteration, requiring no retraining or calibration. It costs at most 2.3% added latency and implementation complexity in the quantized forward pass, while the headline speedup does not exceed BF16 with pre-converted weights, so gains depend on having integer kernels that beat a BF16 baseline. Failure modes include any planner or model variant where error persists across iterations or is not shared across candidates (fixed dither reintroduces the drift), and results are validated mainly on TD-MPC2, DINO-WM, and Meta-World, so transfer to other stacks is unverified. 0 independent implementations, 1 star. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Capacity Allocation at the Source: Sparse Target Optimization for LLM Knowledge Editing
item.description: The method replaces the standard target hidden-state construction in locate-then-edit knowledge editing (e.g., ROME/MEMIT-style pipelines) with an l1-regularized sparse target that prunes nonessential components before parameters are updated. It adds an optimization step for computing each sparse target vector and introduces a regularization hyperparameter, but requires no additional model capacity and runs on a single GPU. If the sparsity level is miscalibrated, the edit may fail to steer the model to the new output or may still interfere with unrelated knowledge, and benefits depend on the base editing method and model. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: test.

item.title: SHADOWPREFILL: Keeping Your Next Model Warm for Per-Step Model Routing in Agentic LLM Serving
item.description: Replaces cold model switches in per-step routed serving (where the KV cache is discarded on every switch and the new model must re-prefill up to ~63K-token contexts) by prefilling the session context on the unchosen model in idle capacity, with shadow KV spilled to host memory. It costs a serving-stack scheduler that harvests per-iteration SLO slack, host-memory KV spill, a 0.4% energy increase, and requires running at least two model instances concurrently, which exceeds a single 24 GB GPU for production-sized models. It can fail when shadow prefills are incomplete (forcing a cold switch anyway), when normal traffic leaves no idle capacity, or when the workload does not use per-step multi-model routing, in which case there is no switch penalty to amortize. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: serving and batching. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: One-Sided Expert-Parallel All-to-All for Mixture-of-Experts Inference over NVLink
item.description: Replaces the two-sided EP all-to-all dispatch/combine stack (e.g., DeepEP) with a one-sided push into rank-major NVLink buffers, letting grouped GEMMs read tokens in place without metadata exchange or per-expert copies. Costs are confined to single-NVLink-domain deployments, a custom synchronization protocol (Fence or Sentinel) that must be integrated into the inference framework, and buffer management across ranks. It fails if the reader lacks multi-GPU NVLink nodes, runs MoE models at large per-GPU batches where the fixed-cost advantage shrinks, or needs portability to non-NVLink interconnects or heterogeneous clusters. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: attention and kernels. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Block-Sparse Gauss-Newton Optimization of Finite Basis Physics-Informed Neural Networks: Sparse Automatic Differentiation Approach
item.description: The method replaces first-order optimizers (e.g., Adam) for training finite-basis physics-informed neural networks with a Gauss-Newton scheme that exploits domain-decomposition-induced block sparsity, using graph coloring to compress Jacobian computation and sparse direct or preconditioned iterative solvers for the Gauss-Newton system. It costs substantial implementation complexity: sparse automatic differentiation infrastructure, graph coloring of Jacobian structure, and sparse linear algebra tooling, none of which are standard components in typical ML stacks. It can fail when the PDE residual problem does not decompose into overlapping subdomains with localized subnetwork influence, when the Gauss-Newton approximation is poor (e.g., far from convergence or non-least-squares structure), or when the problem size is small enough that second-order overhead exceeds any convergence benefit. 0 independent implementations, 1 star. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Decode Token Parallelism: Memory-Efficient Distributed Attention Parallelism for Scalable LLM Decoding
item.description: The method replaces both tensor parallelism (which replicates weights across nodes) and decode context parallelism (which requires cross-node attention merging) by decoupling weight placement from KV cache ownership. It costs increased complexity in orchestrating layer blocks across nodes and requires network bandwidth for current-token activations, though it eliminates cross-node attention aggregation. After adoption, the technique fails if the cluster lacks sufficient NVLink domains or if the workload does not sustain the high-concurrency long-context regime required to amortize the distributed architecture overhead. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: serving and batching. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Stochastic Projections and Rank-Aware Learning Rates for Federated LoRA
item.description: The method replaces standard federated LoRA, in which clients train and transmit both A and B, with a frozen, periodically resampled random A so only B is trained and uploaded, plus learning rates scaled to each client's adaptation rank. It cuts client compute and uplink traffic roughly in half, but requires rank-dependent learning-rate scheduling, coordination of A resampling across rounds, and adds a stochastic projection whose gradient noise grows at low ranks. It can fail when many clients must use very low ranks, when rank heterogeneity makes the rank-scaled learning rates unstable, or when the convergence assumptions do not match non-IID production data; it also presumes a federated setting that single-GPU practitioners may not have. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: An Asynchronous Federated Learning Platform for Lung Adenocarcinoma Grading via Foundation Models and Structural Pruning
item.description: The method replaces centralized multi-institutional pathology training and full-weight federated transmission with a federated system (FedNova) that shares only pruned model weights, using UNI2 features with CLAM-SB. It costs the engineering complexity of operating a multi-client federated web platform and, for most aggregation algorithms, a degradation in Test AUC as pruning sparsity increases. It can fail when participating institutions have heterogeneous data distributions or small local cohorts, when the assumed privacy benefit is undermined by weight leakage, and when pruning interacts poorly with the chosen aggregation algorithm, as observed for FedAvg, FedProx, and FedBN. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Cleaning an Agent's History Hurts When the World Still Holds the Error
item.description: The technique replaces blind history cleaning (compaction, repair, or handoff that rewrites past mistakes as resolved) with edits whose phrasing is checked against the actual world state, such as truthful annotations that preserve the error rather than completed-action claims. It costs added complexity in the compaction pipeline, since the editor must query or track world state before rewriting history, and it offers no latency or memory savings. It can fail when the system cannot verify world state at edit time, because a clean-looking history describing an error the world still holds leaves the continuing agent worse off than an unedited history. 4 independent implementations, 150 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Where Should the Code Go? Locating Foundation-Model Errors in Bitemporal Inventory Simulation
item.description: Replaces free-form LLM reasoning over raw bitemporal reports with exact canonicalization before the model call and exact deterministic rollout after it, in an exactly solvable inventory simulation. Costs engineering effort to build the canonical input layer and exact continuation code, plus interface care since forced-answer calls can disable reasoning or exhaust output budgets on some model-provider pairs. Can fail if the wrong remedy is applied (canonicalization does not fix rollout errors and vice versa), if the model is already at ceiling, or if the tool-calling interface confounds reasoning evaluation. 1 independent implementation, 4 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Together Compiler: Continual Compilation for AI Inference
item.description: TKCC replaces manually tuned kernels and fixed engine configurations with a persistent agent loop that continually compiles and hill-climbs the inference forward pass, using a tiered persistent engine for high-fidelity measurement and a cost model to seed parallelism choices. The cost is substantial engineering complexity: a custom persistent engine layer, agent context management, and continuous compilation infrastructure, plus dependence on proprietary tooling not publicly available. It can fail when workload distributions shift faster than the agent loop converges, when low-fidelity kernel benchmarks mislead optimization for data-dependent operations like MoE routing, or when compiled artifacts overfit to measured traffic and regress under real serving conditions. 1 independent implementation, 129 stars. Research area: attention and kernels. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: UniPipe: Unified Inference Serving and Fine-Tuning for Deadline-Constrained DNN Surrogate Workflows
item.description: UniPipe replaces the common practice of either freezing a pretrained surrogate or running fine-tuning in a separate CUDA context alongside serving, by fusing training and inference samples into one forward pass with a selective backward pass and an offline batch-composition scheduler on a single GPU. The cost is implementation complexity: a custom scheduler exploiting the non-linear latency-versus-batch curve, workload repetitiveness assumptions, and engineering to fuse training and inference batches, with some training throughput traded for latency stability. It can fail when the input stream is not repetitive enough for offline scheduling, when the GPU's latency curve does not exhibit the assumed non-linearity, or when fine-tuning on live data causes drift or instability without validation safeguards. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: serving and batching. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Rational Use of Time for Social Coordination in Humans and AI
item.description: The study replaces explicit-communication coordination protocols with a benchmark (The Mind card game) in which agents must coordinate using only pause timing, comparing 150 humans against computer-use agents and text-prompted LLMs under a Bayesian model of partner-belief inference. It costs nothing to deploy directly, but operationalizing continuous-time cues in production agents adds interface complexity (timestamp capture, latency-sensitive turn handling) that standard text-prompted LLM pipelines do not natively support. The key failure mode is precisely what the paper documents: models can represent a Bayesian-style timing strategy yet fail to adapt to a specific partner across repeated interactions, so systems built on implicit temporal signaling may coordinate poorly in long-horizon or repeated-interaction deployments. 1 independent implementation, 129 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Distributionally Robust BEST-RQ For Speech Representation Learning
item.description: The method replaces uniform averaging of losses across random-projection codebooks in BEST-RQ self-supervised pretraining with KL-regularized group DRO that adaptively upweights poorly performing codebook groups. The cost is additional group-loss tracking, adaptive reweighting logic, and a KL regularization hyperparameter during pretraining, with no inference-time overhead. It can fail if group reweighting destabilizes training, if the KL penalty is miscalibrated, or if gains do not transfer beyond the evaluated multilingual speech setting. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: OverServe: Resource Amplification Attacks on SaaS Agents via Tool--Prompt Co-Design
item.description: The technique replaces indiscriminate agent attacks with a multi-agent co-design that pairs MCP status tools (which return accurate status and terminate normally) with completion-confirmation prompts to exploit the agent's autonomous completion decisions. It costs the attacker the complexity of maintaining a multi-agent framework and separate tool and prompt reviews; for the victim SaaS provider, it increases API request consumption and resource usage without additional customer payment. For a defender, implementing countermeasures (budget caps, loop detection, verification of completion) adds operational overhead. What can fail after adoption of defenses: OverServe's tool specifications trigger no alerts in evaluated MCP scanners, so existing scanning tools may miss these attacks, and agents may still repeatedly check unfinished conditions despite task completion. 1 independent implementation, 8 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Sophon: A Procedural Diagnostic for Spatial Reasoning in Vision-Language Models
item.description: The method replaces wholesale model switching or full fine-tuning of open VLMs for spatial reasoning with targeted LoRA adaptation of mid-stack language-tower layers that route visual features to the readout. It costs a small LoRA training run per architecture plus generation of (or reliance on the authors') procedurally generated paired point-cloud data, with no inference-time memory or latency penalty. It can fail because the repair is demonstrated only on Sophon's synthetic, prior-stripped stimuli, so transfer to real-image spatial tasks is unverified, and gains may not hold across other architectures, LoRA ranks, or target layers. 0 independent implementations, 20 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: AutoAssumption: Searching over Assumptions Discovers ML-Systems Algorithms
item.description: AutoAssumption replaces manual or program-level algorithm search (as in AlphaEvolve/OpenEvolve) with LLM search over explicit assumptions in Lean-checked proof graphs, relaxing one assumption of a published method, re-deriving it, and generating code. It costs the effort of formalizing target algorithms as Lean proof graphs plus LLM search and verification compute, which is a substantial per-domain upfront investment beyond typical inference-engineering workflows. It can fail because a verified proof does not guarantee the generated code is efficient or correct in deployment, the reported gains are specific to the evaluated benchmarks and models, and domains not yet formalized cannot be searched. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Can an AI Agent Be Epistemically Akratic? Higher-Order Evidence & the Limits of Self-Correction
item.description: This is a philosophical analysis, not a method: it argues against the common practice of forcing an agent's conclusions to agree with its own self-assessments of justification, proposing instead that negative self-assessments be used to flag conclusions for further scrutiny rather than to eliminate them. It costs nothing to consider but replaces no concrete pipeline, and offers no implementation, metric, or empirical evaluation. What can fail if applied naively is a self-correction loop trained or prompted for conclusion-assessment agreement, which the paper argues can be achieved by degrading either the reasoning or the assessment rather than improving reliability. 1 independent implementation, 125 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: SubGPU Pipelining: Intra-GPU Fine-Grained Spatial Parallelism for LLM Inference
item.description: This technique replaces temporal (sequential) kernel execution with spatial partitioning of the GPU's streaming multiprocessors into pipeline stages. It requires B200-class hardware with CUDA Green Contexts and involves complex co-optimization of graph cuts, SM allocation, and microbatch sizing. Failure risks include workload misalignment with the pipeline structure and suboptimal shared-resource contention if the segmentation is not precisely tuned to the specific model architecture. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: attention and kernels. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: MuEdit: An efficient multi-task editing method towards inter-domain knowledge conflicts
item.description: Replaces naive sequential application of single-task editing methods (e.g., null-space-constrained editors such as MEMIT-style updates) with conflict-aware task ordering plus dynamic low-rank approximation to expand the common null space. Costs an additional ordering step, a conflict-index computation, and per-edit low-rank factors rather than single updates; editing remains cheap relative to fine-tuning but adds implementation complexity. Fails when task Jacobians share almost no null space so that even expanded low-rank directions cannot accommodate conflict-free updates, and benefits may not transfer to backbones or domains beyond the five tested. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: ToolTurns: Benchmarking LLM Agents in Multi-Turn Dialogue
item.description: This benchmark replaces single-turn tool-use evaluations with multi-turn dialogues that test clarification, tool use, and context retention. It requires implementing or adopting the open-source user simulator and checker--fixer pipeline, which adds evaluation complexity and compute overhead. The method can fail if the user simulator does not accurately reflect real user behavior or if the checker--fixer introduces biases in turn revision. 3 independent implementations, 145 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: RSI-PDEbench: A Benchmark for Self-Improving Agents in PDE Solving
item.description: The RSI-PDE harness replaces manual expert workflows for PDE equation discovery, coefficient estimation, and solver configuration, and improves on single-run LLM prompting and unmodified native agent harnesses. It costs the engineering effort of implementing the residual-loss shortlisting, relative-L2 feedback loop, and validation gate on top of frontier API models, with the benchmarked gains specific to the PDE-solving domain. It can fail on noisy or out-of-distribution equation templates where pass rates remain lower, and the validation gate may not transfer to domains without a computable residual or verification signal. 1 independent implementation, 126 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: JoyFrontBench: Evaluating Front-End Coding Agents through Goal-Oriented Acceptance Contracts
item.description: JoyFrontBench replaces aggregate task scoring with goal-oriented acceptance contracts that require all mandatory criteria to pass for application success. It costs the implementation effort of defining explicit acceptance criteria and running evidence-grounded evaluations instead of relying on automated metrics. It can fail if the acceptance contracts do not fully capture production requirements or if the evaluation harness introduces environment-specific inconsistencies. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Termination Lag: Coding Agents Solve Early but Stop Late
item.description: The paper is a measurement study, not a deployable method: it characterizes termination lag by testing every intermediate patch, which replaces nothing directly but motivates early-stopping or patch-checkpointing policies in place of fixed step budgets. Adopting an early-stop or best-patch-selection policy costs a per-step patch-evaluation harness (test execution per candidate patch) plus policy-tuning complexity. It can fail because stopping at the first test-passing patch risks accepting an incomplete or overfit solution, while continuing risks regressions in the 1-8% of runs where agents undo correct work. 1 independent implementation, 125 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: test.

item.title: FIRE: Failure Isolation and Reliability for Production-Connected Experiments at Scale
item.description: The method replaces isolated pre-production testing with production-connected replay traffic that uses isolated tiers, dependency monitors, and traffic pinning. It requires maintaining replicated ranking tiers, dedicated downstream workers for traffic pinning, and continuous monitoring infrastructure. Failures can occur if isolation is incomplete, monitors malfunction, or resource constraints limit the designated worker subset, potentially affecting production services. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: EvoX: Rethinking the Agent Harness as a Runtime Policy
item.description: EvoX replaces the implicit, prompt-only orchestration logic of conventional agent harnesses with a Rust-based runtime that deterministically enforces action realization, execution continuity, and outcome grounding alongside the model's own decisions. It costs an additional runtime layer (Rust service deployment and maintenance), constrains the harness to specific tool-call and verification semantics, and its gains are model-dependent, averaging only ~3 points overall. It can fail when tasks depend on memory or extensions the runtime deliberately omits, when its deterministic controls misjudge legitimate completion claims, or when a provider's API behavior diverges from the verified request patterns. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: failure recovery. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Science Prediction Universe
item.description: SPU is an evaluation benchmark of 100 public and 16 private wet-lab experimental-outcome prediction tasks; it replaces informal or proxy-based assessment of scientific agents, not any production component. Adoption costs nothing to run directly since it is an evaluation artifact, but reproducing the study's setup (frontier API models under Codex or Claude Code harnesses, hundreds of thousands of tool calls) carries real API spend, and the private-task split is not accessible. The findings themselves are the actionable signal: frontier agents achieve only 0.227-0.478 task-adjusted Spearman correlation, agree with each other (0.52) far more than with experimental reality (0.33), and compute trivial proxies that do not affect outcomes, so deploying an LLM agent for experimental-outcome ranking today would fail precisely on the scientific-judgment dimension that matters. 1 independent implementation, 134 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: WordInferBench: Can Agents Infer How to Edit from Word Document Context?
item.description: This benchmark replaces fully specified document-editing instructions with 280 base instances evaluated under descriptive, referential, and inferential conditions across 13 object types and 81 attributes. It costs access to capable coding-agent systems and an evaluation setup rather than training or dedicated infrastructure, and it adds benchmark complexity without by itself improving production editing quality. It can fail to transfer if its Common Crawl-derived Word documents, exemplar-recoverable formatting assumptions, or agent harness do not match the reader's production documents and workflows. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Pre-QED: Environment Specifications for Agentic Verification
item.description: The method replaces shallow specifications such as reused fuzz harnesses, whose proofs cover only a single call sequence, with executable verification harnesses that model all legal API usages, with illegal call orders excluded via Linear-time Temporal Logic constraints extracted by an agentic workflow from code and documentation. The cost is substantial: constructing deep environment specifications requires an agentic extraction pipeline plus formal-methods expertise, and proving the resulting harnesses is itself an open challenge the authors explicitly release to the community rather than solve. Adoption can fail because the extracted usage contract may be incomplete or incorrect, making the proof cover the wrong specification, and because current provers may simply be unable to discharge the harness proofs. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: guardscope: Measuring Which Actions Runtime Controls Check in LLM Agent Systems
item.description: guardscope replaces trusting a runtime control's marketing or documentation claims about which agent action paths it inspects with a static-plus-empirical audit that reconciles the control's decision records against kernel-level ground truth, classifying each action as checked, bypassed, or prevented. It costs the engineering effort to instrument deployments with kernel-level tracing, run the fixed workload across one of eight topology designs, and integrate the framework into your agent harness, plus the latency inherent in any runtime control you choose to verify. It can fail if your production topology differs from the tested designs, if kernel-level instrumentation is unavailable or restricted in your environment (e.g., managed containers), or if a control's coverage holds under the fixed workload but breaks under your actual traffic patterns. 1 independent implementation, 130 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: CastWorld: Benchmarking Context-Aware Agentic Time Series Forecasting Beyond Predictive Accuracy
item.description: CastWorld replaces ad hoc accuracy-only evaluation of forecasting agents with a benchmark harness providing 25 contextual datasets, 49 forecasting tools, and trajectory- and version-history-based assessment of forecast quality, process, trustworthiness, and resource use. Adoption costs integration effort against its context specification and harness, plus API or GPU budget to run iterative agent loops, and it evaluates rather than improves a production forecaster. Its own findings indicate the failure modes: additional interaction rounds do not necessarily improve forecasts, and agents can fail to select their best previously generated prediction, so more agentic complexity can be neutral or harmful. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Knowledge in the Harness, Reliability in the Weights: Teacher-Free Co-Evolution of an LLM Agent
item.description: Replaces hand-written system-prompt policies and teacher-model distillation with on-demand skill files that the model itself extends from deployment logs, gated by code checks and self-review, plus GRPO LoRA training on logged conversations. Costs a RL training pipeline (GRPO with LoRA, feasible on a single 24 GB GPU for 12B-scale models only with careful memory management), a validation-gate infrastructure for rule admission, and logged task outcomes; latency impact is small since skills are retrieved on demand. Can fail when deployment logs lack reference outcomes, when self-written rules pass the gates but encode wrong policy, and because gains were shown only on two tau2-bench domains and may not transfer. 4 independent implementations, 152 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Where Autonomy Belongs: A Separation of Powers for Agentic Program Evolution
item.description: EvoTrias replaces monolithic agent-centric evolution loops, where one coding agent both governs the search and proposes candidates, with a three-owner architecture (Structured Governance, Open Proposal, Protected Judgment) that exchanges only typed contracts and can wrap an existing coding agent as a plugin. The cost is additional orchestration complexity: three coordinated components, contract schemas, runtime boundary hooks, and a private evaluator that must be maintained and kept isolated from the proposing agent. What can fail is the judgment boundary in practice, since the Protected Judgment guarantee depends on the evaluator staying private and representative, and the 64% token saving and benchmark gains were measured on the authors' setup and may not transfer to a small team's codebase and budget without workload-specific validation. 1 independent implementation, 125 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: test.

item.title: SimRec: Learning to Search, Ask, and Recommend from Simulated Interaction
item.description: SimRec replaces hand-designed recommendation workflows and component-wise training (query rewriting, list ranking) with end-to-end GRPO reinforcement learning over the full interaction trajectory, using a task-anchored user simulator and a trajectory-level reward with training-only target injection. The cost is a full RL training pipeline: a user simulator (external LLM or self-play), reward engineering across retrieval quality, tool validity, and final hit, and GRPO rollouts, which exceeds inference-only constrained setups in compute and engineering complexity though the resulting 4B model itself fits a 24 GB GPU. It can fail when the simulated user's feedback distribution diverges from real users, when target injection biases the policy toward synthetic shortcuts, or when the reward does not transfer to catalogs and query distributions beyond ESCI and Amazon C4. 2 independent implementations, 37 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Recompute or Restore? Host-Tier KV for Multi-Model Agent Workflows on a Static-Graph NPU Serving Stack
item.description: The method replaces prefix KV recomputation with restore from a synchronous host-DRAM tier, avoiding repeated prefill (89.5% of planner prompt tokens had been materialized before). The cost is host DRAM for the tier plus transfer time that occupies the same engine thread as prefill and decode, causing a measured 16-18% P99 latency increase for fork workflows. Benefits are seed-sensitive for mixed and bursty workloads, the gain is demonstrated only on a specific commercial static-graph NPU stack (Rebellions ATOM+, vllm-rbln), and the predictive model misorders three policy contrasts. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Read Once, Answer Many: Parallel Prompting for Shared-Context LLM Inference
item.description: The method replaces prefix caching plus per-question decoding, in which every decode step re-reads the shared document's KV cache once per question, by decoding P questions as P independent streams of a single request with a stream-id attention mask inside the kernel, so the document is read once per step for all streams. The cost is a forked SGLang (about 80 lines across three files plus a small engine package), fixed-shape decode steps required for CUDA-graph capture, and applicability only to workloads with many independent questions over one long document. It can fail if the workload does not share a long context across queries, if stream counts are too small to amortize the fused step, if the mask is misapplied and answers leak across streams, or if the patch diverges from upstream SGLang releases and becomes a maintenance burden. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: serving and batching. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Bit-Sparsity Aware Acceleration with Compact CSD Code on Generic Matrix Multiplication
item.description: The method replaces conventional bit-parallel matrix-multiplication datapaths with a custom ASIC using compact canonical-signed-digit (CCSD) on-chip sparsification and segmented dot products for FP and QINT operands. It costs custom silicon design and fabrication at the RTL/process-node level, which a single 24 GB GPU or API-based workflow cannot use, emulate meaningfully, or procure. The gains may fail to transfer to commodity GPUs, and the claimed speedups are relative to a research accelerator (Bitlet), not to cuBLAS-class libraries readers actually run. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: attention and kernels. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: MAST: Medoid-Anchored Subspace Steering for Visual Grounding in Multimodal LLMs
item.description: MAST replaces global-mean activation steering in multimodal LLMs with training-free, input-adaptive steering that routes each query to clustered task medoids and aggregates low-rank local directions; MAST-PR adds a lightweight probe to reweight task-specialized direction families. It costs offline clustering and medoid storage per task, plus per-query routing, subspace extraction, and optional probe inference, while adding pipeline complexity without reported latency or memory figures. It can fail if task clusters are unstable, routing mismatches queries, local low-rank directions do not transfer across models or datasets, or the probe introduces task-aware overfitting and serving fragility. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: efficient architectures. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Sparse Matrix Multiplication Exponent 1.5 in the Low-bandwidth Model
item.description: This is a theoretical result in distributed computing: it replaces prior multi-party algorithms for multiplying uniformly sparse matrices under a one-message-per-round bandwidth constraint. It assumes n computers, globally known sparsity structure, and offers no implementation, constants, or empirical evaluation; the cost is a distributed cluster the reader does not have. Nothing here transfers to single-GPU inference, API-based serving, or sparse kernels, so adoption failure is moot because there is nothing deployable to adopt. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: TQIR: Trellis Quantization with Integer Reconstruction for Bandwidth-Efficient Edge LLM Acceleration
item.description: TQIR replaces floating-point trellis weight decoding with offline trellis matching constrained to exact INT8/INT4 codewords, enabling integer GEMM with reduced weight-memory traffic, and moves the reverse Hadamard transform to the activation side. It requires algorithm-hardware co-design, including a custom decoder block, subspace Hadamard transform, and compatible integer-GEMM runtime, so adoption costs implementation complexity beyond a typical software-only quantization workflow. It can fail for teams without custom silicon or specialized kernel support, and gains may not transfer if model accuracy, memory bandwidth, or deployment hardware differ from the evaluated setting. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Sub-100KB On-Device CNN Training via Dynamic Sparse Updates and Hardware--Software Co-Design
item.description: Replaces full-precision off-device training and standard activation storage with a hardware-software co-design using dynamic sparse updates and FP8 on-chip processing. Costs include reliance on custom TSMC 28nm silicon, lower-precision arithmetic, and reduced model accuracy potential from aggressive pruning. Can fail when applied to workloads requiring high model capacity, where hardware manufacturing is unavailable, or when the sparse update mechanism degrades convergence stability. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Communication-Efficient Federated Multi-View Clustering via View-Aware Quantization
item.description: The method replaces full-precision transmission of high-dimensional client representations with dynamically bit-assigned quantized representations under a global bit budget, where quantization bits are allocated by iteratively updated view importance scores. It costs additional client- and server-side logic for importance estimation and bit allocation, plus integration effort into an existing FedMVC pipeline, with a bounded risk of clustering quality loss from quantization error. It can fail when view importance estimates are noisy or unstable early in training, when heterogeneity across clients makes a shared bit budget poorly calibrated, or when the deployment is not actually a federated multi-view clustering system, in which case nothing here transfers. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: LLMRunner: Closed Workload Model Performance Testing Framework for LLM Servings
item.description: LLMRunner replaces open-loop benchmarking with closed workload testing that simulates realistic multi-turn conversations and user think-times. It requires implementing conversational state tracking and declarative experiment matrices, adding complexity to the testing pipeline. The UVM finding applies only to non-oversubscription scenarios and may not hold when GPU memory is oversubscribed or with different model architectures. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: serving and batching. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: Read and Ignore: What Self-Directed LLM Agents Do in Public Service Scenarios
item.description: Replaces ad-hoc prompt review or vendor benchmarking with a rule-based evaluation of agent trajectories on an institution's own records and scenarios, requiring no labeled data or model retraining. Cost is limited to API or local inference calls for trajectory collection plus scenario construction; the taxonomy and released code keep infrastructure demands within a single GPU or API budget. It can fail if the four scenario templates do not match the deployed workflow, since models may pass bounded tests yet still ignore records or produce artifacts contradicting them in settings the taxonomy does not cover. 1 independent implementation, 4 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: SkillEarth: Teaching General-Purpose Agents to Act on Earth via Skill Evolution
item.description: SkillEarth replaces manually authored tool-call prompts, predefined expert knowledge, and parameter retraining with reusable skill files automatically extracted from demonstrated trajectories and refined through real tool-chain execution feedback plus a dual-judge routing graph. The cost is added pipeline complexity: trajectory collection, execution-grounded refinement loops, judge model calls, and a skill retrieval and versioning layer that must be maintained in production. It can fail if extracted skills overfit to demonstrated trajectories and misroute on novel tasks, if judge feedback encodes errors into skills, or if the remote-sensing results do not transfer to the reader's tool domain. 1 independent implementation, 129 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: test.

item.title: DecArena: Evaluating Large-Scale Decentralized Multi-Agent Collaboration
item.description: Replaces a centralized global orchestrator (and naive decentralized agents without discovery) with graph-constrained routing: a topology-aware warmup phase plus self-improving LLM-based neighbor routing for tool discovery across 100K+ distributed tools. Costs include extra warmup interactions, multi-hop message latency across the graph, per-hop LLM routing inference, and implementation complexity for graph maintenance and routing-state updates. It can fail on dynamic or sparse topologies where routing degrades, the paper shows standard RL does not fix discovery, and the synthetic benchmark plus unspecified GraphHarness inference overhead leave production transfer unverified. 0 independent implementations, 3 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: GHAgentCI: A Dataset of Coding-Agent Invocations in CI Workflow Histories
item.description: This is a mining dataset and extractor (cai-miner) cataloguing how coding agents are integrated into GitHub Actions workflows, replacing ad hoc manual identification of agentic CI patterns with a validated, longitudinal corpus of 15K+ workflow histories. It imposes no production cost because it is a research artifact rather than a deployable method, though using the extractor requires running repository mining at whatever scale the reader needs. Detection precision varies by evidence kind (96.1% for dedicated actions, 98.8% for GitHub Agentic Workflows, lower for other kinds), so findings built on noisier evidence categories can misclassify workflows. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Faithful in Steps: Improving Generalization and Citation in RAG via Query Decomposition
item.description: The technique replaces single-pass attributed RAG (RAGQ), where the model retrieves and cites contexts directly for the full question, with a pipeline that decomposes the question into atomic subquestions to resolve implicit entities, then uses a reranker to prune distractor contexts and reduce over-citation. It costs an additional decomposition step (either zero-shot prompting of an MLLM or a fine-tuned decomposer), extra retrieval and reranking passes per query, and added pipeline latency and orchestration complexity relative to a single retrieve-and-generate call. Failure modes include decomposition errors propagating into wrong subquestion retrieval, residual over-citation if the reranker thresholds are miscalibrated, and dependence on a capable multimodal LLM that may exceed the reader's local GPU budget and require paid API access. 1 independent implementation, 125 stars. Research area: retrieval and RAG. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Can We Make an LLM Dumber, or Is It Just Playing Dumb? An Empirical Study of Believable Performance Throttling
item.description: This method replaces prompting, temperature scaling, and weight noise for deliberately reducing model performance to a target benchmark score. It requires training a LoRA adapter with weak-teacher data, adding training cost and deployment complexity. It can fail by converging to an answer-token attractor on multiple choice (up to 97% of new errors on one letter), transferring poorly across benchmarks (14.2-point error), and producing detectable error patterns despite local plausibility. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: TraceKV: Policy-Preserving Low-Rank KV Cache Compression for Reasoning Vision-Language Models
item.description: TraceKV replaces full-precision dense KV cache storage for reasoning VLMs with sensitivity-aware low-rank latent representations calibrated on on-policy reasoning states, plus a global rank allocation and custom low-rank attention kernels. It is training-free, but adoption costs integration of on-policy calibration, per-layer rank configuration, and nonstandard attention kernels into the serving stack, with residual accuracy risk from policy drift if calibration diverges from deployment workloads. It can fail when production reasoning traces differ from calibration states, when the target model lacks a supported kernel path, or when stacking with quantization compounds approximation error beyond the near-lossless regime reported. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Bug Finding With Agentic Symbolic Execution
item.description: It replaces manual assertion annotation and hand-written environment models for symbolic execution with an LLM agent that instruments code, synthesizes a constraint-aware database environment, and generates a reproducing test per bug. Costs are LLM API spend per repository analysis, the engineering effort to integrate CrossHair and the harness into CI, and restriction to Python codebases amenable to symbolic execution. It can fail on code outside CrossHair's modeling capacity (native extensions, complex I/O, concurrency), produce environment models that admit false positives, and its crash-oriented findings complement rather than replace wrong-output bug detection. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: test.

item.title: MemCredit: From Relevance to Utility for Decision-Time Memory in Long-Horizon Web Agents
item.description: The method replaces semantic-relevance ranking for context pruning with a lightweight utility estimator distilled from counterfactual interventions, using relevance only for candidate generation. It requires an offline training phase involving controlled environment interactions to estimate marginal memory contributions, adding pipeline complexity and training compute before deployment. The approach can fail if the utility estimator generalizes poorly across task distributions or if the credit assignment process is too computationally expensive for the reader's limited budget. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: The Noise Floor of a Quantization Comparison: Engine, restart, batch and kernel drift, measured against 8-bit and 4-bit effects in two decision models
item.description: This methodology replaces aggregate accuracy comparison by measuring decision-level changes against a baseline noise floor encompassing engine restarts, batching variations, and kernel selection differences. It requires recording per-sample outputs across multiple inference runs and engine configurations, adding engineering overhead to the evaluation pipeline. Reliance on aggregate metrics can fail to detect substantial per-decision regressions—such as 436 degraded decisions offset by improvements elsewhere—leading to deployment of models that appear stable but alter behavior on individual inputs. 2 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: DISCERN: Preserve at Write, Resolve at Read for Persistent LLM-Agent Memory
item.description: DISCERN replaces conventional RAG-style memory retrieval (embedding search over merged or overwritten memory entries) with a strictly additive bi-temporal provenance graph written without merging entities or dropping superseded values, plus a zero-LLM tool surface that an agentic loop navigates to commit one of four gated terminal actions, including abstention. The cost is implementation complexity: a custom graph schema, write-time provenance instrumentation, and a read-time navigation loop with more orchestration steps and thus higher per-query latency than a single vector lookup, though it runs within a single-GPU or API-only budget since the tool surface itself uses no LLM calls. It can fail if the write-time extraction of entities and time-states is noisy, since errors accumulate in an append-only graph that is never corrected, and the headline gains are demonstrated on a 310-query synthetic benchmark, so real-world entity-resolution and abstention benefits remain unvalidated. 2 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: test.

item.title: MULTILOOP: Evolving Multi-Agent Harnesses for Complex Information-Seeking Tasks
item.description: Replaces hand-tuned multi-agent prompts and orchestration logic with a coding-agent loop that analyzes execution traces and edits the harness automatically. Costs iterative LLM calls for trace analysis and code editing, plus evaluation runs, and adds a meta-optimization layer of complexity over an already multi-component system. Orchestration failures specific to multi-agent systems, such as poor delegation and information sharing, largely persist after optimization, so gains may be limited to per-agent behavior fixes rather than structural coordination improvements. 1 independent implementation, 24 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: test.

item.title: VibePrevisBench: Evaluating Agentic Coding for 4D Scene Generation in Blender
item.description: VibePrevisBench replaces ad hoc, demo-based judgment of coding agents for controllable video generation with 242 scored tasks combining rule-based scene verification and VLM-based render judging. It costs nothing to adopt computationally since it is an evaluation artifact, but using it requires Blender execution infrastructure and VLM judge access, and it addresses a narrow workflow (graybox proxy video generation). It can fail as a selection tool if the reader's production tasks differ from script-to-4D-scene reconstruction, and its VLM-based Screen Check inherits judge subjectivity and may not transfer to other visual domains. 1 independent implementation, 30 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Sparse PCA with Overlapping Supports: NP-Hardness and an FPTAS
item.description: This algorithmic technique replaces heuristic or exponential-time methods for multi-component Sparse PCA with overlapping supports and exact orthogonality constraints. It requires solving a reduced sparse orthogonal Procrustes problem via approximate dynamic programming and algebraic number representation, with runtime exponential in the fixed rank and number of components. It can fail to be practical when the rank or component count grows, as the complexity depends exponentially on these parameters, and it does not address approximate orthogonality or large-scale covariance matrices. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Controlling the Probability of Unknown Unknowns in Pre-Deployment Testing of AI Systems
item.description: The method replaces heuristic or fixed-horizon Good-Turing stopping rules with an anytime-valid upper confidence sequence for the probability of observing an unseen failure mode. Its cost is additional statistical machinery, dependence on repeated test execution and labeling, and more complex decision logic than a single final evaluation. It can fail if automated failure labels are biased or inconsistent, if the test distribution shifts from deployment, or if the assumed sampling and confidence conditions are violated. 2 independent implementations, 2128 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Spec-Driven PBT: Deriving Semantic Invariants from Code Specifications for Agentic Property-based Testing
item.description: It replaces deriving test invariants solely from the implementation by first extracting natural-language invariants from the product specification and then using the code to translate them into executable property tests. The cost is an additional specification-analysis step plus dependence on a sufficiently detailed specification and an LLM agent pipeline for test generation. It can fail when specifications are incomplete or ambiguous, when generated properties are not executable or faithful, and when implementation-robustness bugs remain better covered by code-driven testing. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: test.

item.title: NVIDIA Vera: A Microarchitecture-Level Comparison with Grace, Turin, and Granite Rapids
item.description: The paper does not propose a technique; it benchmarks NVIDIA's Vera CPU against AMD Turin, Intel Granite Rapids, and Grace across microbenchmarks, NAS kernels, and scientific codes. It replaces nothing in an ML engineer's stack; procurement of next-generation data-center CPUs is outside the reader's constrained infrastructure, which consists of one 24 GB GPU or third-party APIs. Vera trails Intel and AMD in some compute-bound floating-point workloads, reflecting NVIDIA's GPU focus for such tasks. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: PhysICL: In-Context Learning of Physical Fields on Unstructured Meshes from Procedural Priors
item.description: The method replaces per-study surrogate retraining on unstructured-mesh simulations with a single checkpoint that infers new field-prediction tasks in context from labeled simulations, but adopting it requires pretraining on procedurally generated tasks (or fine-tuning an existing checkpoint if one is released), which is a training investment outside a no-training budget. Costs are modest at inference (about 4.3 GiB at K=64 on million-node meshes, within a 24 GB GPU), but pretraining is the dominant expense and no public checkpoint or PLAID-scale pretrained weights are guaranteed. It can fail where the target physics is far from the procedural prior (accuracy lagged reduced-order models on low-rank fields) and it needed prior-matched fine-tuning to reach acceptable stress error on 2D_MSHE. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Fit-LRP: Fitting Linear Relaxations to Polytopes for Neural Network Verification over Non-Convex Regions
item.description: Fit-LRP replaces loose axis-aligned box relaxations in the final optimization step of LiRPA/alpha,beta-CROWN verification with exact affine bounds over unions of polytopes, solved as a sequence of small low-dimensional linear programs. The cost is added LP-solving per verification node and the need to formulate specifications as explicit polyhedral regions, with reported speedups of up to 15x in worst-case verification time and large reductions in branching. It can fail when specifications are not naturally polyhedral, when LP overhead outweighs pruning gains on easy instances, or when the surrounding BaB pipeline and reachability tooling are not already in place. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: KVPath: Connecting Key-Value Representations Across Transformer Layers
item.description: KVPath replaces the standard per-layer independent KV cache with a single full-dimensional base KV at the first layer plus compact low-dimensional delta KVs at subsequent layers (residual or rolling updates) to reconstruct layer-specific states. The cost is architectural: it requires training the model with this parameterization and custom cache-management kernels, so it cannot be retrofitted to existing pretrained checkpoints; the low-dimensional deltas also add reconstruction compute at inference. It can fail if the inter-layer correlation assumption weakens for some model families or scales, degrading quality, and the claimed gains are under matched parameter counts rather than on standard pretrained models, so real-world benefit depends on adoption by model providers. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Trained on What Screen Readers Cannot Read: Accessibility Debt in the GUI Corpora Behind Computer-Use Agents
item.description: It replaces the assumption that captured accessibility trees are complete labels, by measuring content-description coverage and selection bias in GUI corpora. It costs only metadata auditing and element-to-action resolution on existing datasets, with no extra GPU training. It can fail if coding rules, app sampling, or hint-text conventions are misread as universal label quality, so downstream fixes may target the wrong gap. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: ADAPT: Agentic Diff-Aware Patch Testing for Pull Requests
item.description: This method replaces traditional test generation techniques that optimize for broad code coverage rather than the specific behavior introduced in a pull request. It costs the inference fees of an API-based coding agent and the CI compute required to iteratively execute candidate tests against both the base and head versions. Adoption can fail if the repository lacks the necessary isolated execution environments to safely and automatically run agent-generated code, or if the agent's API costs exceed the allocated budget. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: Robo-SWE: An Executable Issue-Resolution Dataset Mined from Robot Software Repositories
item.description: Robo-SWE replaces ad hoc or general-purpose benchmarks (such as SWE-bench-style tasks) for evaluating coding agents on robotics software, providing 236 executable issue-resolution tasks with containers, developer fixes, and fail-to-pass tests. It costs the effort of building and running per-repository containers at pinned commits and requires execution infrastructure to run tests offline; no model training is needed, but reproducing ROS 2 and physics-engine environments is nontrivial. It can fail as an evaluation proxy because task validity is execution-verified but fairness is not human-reviewed, and the 236-task sample across 28 repositories may not represent a given team's stack, so agent rankings may not transfer. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: SwarmSafe-Delta: Isolating Message Effects on LLM Agent Safety
item.description: Replaces aggregate-outcome safety testing with a controlled paired executable protocol that isolates whether upstream messages change executor actions by freezing computation and varying delivery modes. Costs include implementation of deterministic policy states, preassigned budgets, and format-matched placebo construction, plus the need to run multiple paired scenarios rather than simple end-to-end evaluation. Can fail if applied to natural traffic without recognizing it measures constructed information dependencies, not natural failure rates, and results may not generalize across different message compositions or model behaviors. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: JudgeMix: Judge-Guided Mixed-Rollout Data Synthesis for LLM Agents
item.description: JudgeMix replaces random expert-intervention heuristics and uniform step-wise expert supervision in agentic SFT data synthesis with judge-guided selective expert intervention and reweighted supervision. It costs additional inference and orchestration complexity because the pipeline needs target-model rollouts, expert rollouts, and step-wise semantic judging. It can fail if the judge is biased or inaccurate, the expert behavior does not transfer to the target model, or the added synthesis and evaluation overhead is too large for the team's budget. 0 independent implementations, 20 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: SBA: A Practical Memory Performance Denial-of-Service Attack
item.description: IQ-MemGuard replaces bandwidth-centric memory isolation mechanisms such as Intel RDT MBA with a software regulator that detects sustained single-bank DRAM contention via microarchitectural signals and selectively throttles pathological request injection. It costs deployment and tuning of a low-level OS/hypervisor-layer component plus minor throttling overhead on flagged workloads, with no model-level changes. It can fail on platforms lacking the required performance counters, under new attack patterns that avoid detection signals, and the defense is validated only on one Intel platform while the attack itself spans DDR5 and HBM2E systems. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Guided Generation of Linux Kernel Semantic Patches with Small Local Language Models
item.description: This method replaces the manual, months-long conversion of hundreds of Linux kernel drivers when an API changes, specifically substituting hand-written Coccinelle semantic patches with a guided generation framework that decomposes examples into change variants, applies deterministic repairs, and uses a compile critic. It costs the implementation complexity of a script-based decomposer, SmPL syntax repair components, and a compilation feedback loop, requiring a domain-specific toolchain (Coccinelle) and incurring the latency of iterative generation and compilation for each variant. It can fail when general-purpose models produce weak results even with guidance (at most 12 solved), when the greedy rule composition misses correct combinations, or when the deterministic name generalisation fails to abstract driver-specific identifiers correctly. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: What Can a VLA Learn from the Agent That Calls It? Task-Level Experience Distillation for Embodied Navigation
item.description: Replaces the per-episode LLM planner at inference by distilling successful agent trajectories into the VLA via low-rank adaptation, with loss masking on counterproductive steps and stop labels near the goal. Costs include LoRA fine-tuning of an 8B VLA (feasible on a 24 GB GPU), collection of agent session logs, and dependence on the REVERIE-CE embodied navigation setting. Can fail if agent sessions are unavailable, if the masked-heuristic mislabels useful detours, or when deploying outside embodied navigation where no VLA exists. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: distillation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Low Language Transfer Speech-to-Text
item.description: Replaces training a speech recognizer from scratch (or collecting large in-language corpora) for a low-resource language with light fine-tuning, ideally LoRA adapters on a frozen encoder, of an existing open multilingual ASR model on as few as 25-1,000 clips. Costs: a dev set selecting every epoch, roughly 5.7 CER points of degradation on the model's original high-resource languages in the median model, and a word language model for a further 1.2-1.4 CER points on CTC heads. Failure modes: WER remains high (34.4 at best) despite good CER; CTC heads need 20-30 epochs versus 3-5 for seq2seq decoders; and language identification errors can trigger unwanted translation of code-switched speech, as Whisper large-v3's Malay WER rose from 8.9 to 14.9 when told the language. 1 independent implementation, 125 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: Eliciting and Mitigating Specification Satisficing in Coding Agents
item.description: SatisFix replaces generic self-correction or reflection loops with a two-step prompt procedure in which the coding agent first reports implementation choices where it knowingly deviated from a requirement and the reason, then verifies each choice against the task description. It costs additional inference passes per task (more tokens and latency through the same API or local model, no extra infrastructure) plus prompt-engineering integration into an existing agent framework. It can fail when the agent does not actually report its satisficing choices, when the checking step is biased toward the same rationalizations the paper identifies, and gains may not transfer to task types or backbones beyond those evaluated. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Rasoi: Visual Diffs for Evaluating Structural Changes Made by Coding Agents
item.description: Rasoi replaces manual inspection of raw textual diffs after coding-agent edits with visual diffs that show which architectural elements and relationships were added, modified, or removed across abstraction levels. It costs the effort of building or adopting an architecture-extraction and visualization layer on top of existing diff tooling; it is a design probe from a 12-developer qualitative study, not a shipped product, so adopting it means implementing the capability in-house. It can fail if the inferred architecture model is inaccurate or incomplete for a given codebase, if the extra abstraction level overwhelms rather than clarifies on large changes, or if developers over-rely on the visualization and skip verifying actual runtime behavior. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Wanda-Guided Sparse Perturbations for Efficient Zeroth-Order Optimization
item.description: WIS-MeZO replaces MeZO's dense random perturbations in zeroth-order fine-tuning with sparse perturbations restricted to coordinates selected by Wanda weight-activation saliency, while keeping the pretrained weights dense. It adds a one-time saliency computation and mask construction, requires storing a sparse mask, and retains ZO's multiple forward passes per step; claimed benefit is fewer optimization steps to reach comparable validation loss. It can fail if the saliency-ranked support captures insufficient gradient energy for a given task, if the task-conditioning assumption breaks under distribution shift, or if sparse-gather overhead erodes the step-count savings in a memory-bound forward-only pipeline. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Climate Temporal Temperature Prediction via an Adaptive Stacked Bidirectional Residual Mamba Network
item.description: Deep DualMamba replaces Transformer-based attention and MLP layers with an adaptive bidirectional state-space architecture plus a hardware-aware parallel recurrent algorithm. It reduces asymptotic complexity to linear in sequence length at the cost of implementing and validating a custom parallel scan operator and accepting the loss of convolutional efficiency the authors explicitly note. Long-term forecasting can still fail because the method is evaluated only on UK meteorological-station data, the claimed robustness is supported by a single domain, and the abstract supplies no error metrics, baseline deltas, or throughput measurements. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient architectures. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: DRAMA: Dissecting Attention Redundancy for Accelerating Multimodal Diffusion Large Language Models
item.description: DRAMA replaces full-sequence bidirectional attention over all visual tokens with Spatial-Redundancy-Aware Visual Token Pruning (SVTP) and Sufficiency-Guided Adaptive Stopping (SGAS). It requires no training, architectural modification, or attention caching, but introduces inference-time computation for probing attention tensors and dynamic token selection. Accuracy may degrade on benchmarks where the sparse visual token subset or early stopping criteria fail to capture necessary information. 0 independent implementations, 3 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: test.

item.title: IsharaBART: An efficient BART-Based Framework for Low-Resource Bangla Sign Language Translation
item.description: It replaces fine-tuning a large multilingual foundation model with a small BART pre-trained from scratch on domain monolingual text, augmented via rule-based transforms, masked substitution, back-translation, and one-shot prompting. The cost is assembling monolingual corpora, building an annotated parallel set (here 1,000 pairs expanded to 4,831), running a from-scratch pre-training phase, and accepting that full fine-tuning—not LoRA—is needed to preserve quality. It can fail because results are demonstrated only on BdSL gloss translation with a small evaluation set, BLEU gains may not transfer to other low-resource tasks or languages, and the augmentation pipeline can introduce label noise. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Beyond Compressing Everything: Contrastive Memory Learning for Selective Context Compression
item.description: CoMem replaces indiscriminate soft context compression (which encodes all content into fixed memory slots regardless of query) with a query-conditioned compressor trained via contrastive learning on same-document negative queries, using bidirectional attention among memory slots. It costs training a compressor model with specialized hard-negative mining (pairing documents with multiple queries), adds inference-time query encoding before compression, and requires maintaining bidirectional attention infrastructure. It can fail when queries arrive after compression (the method assumes query availability at compression time), when training data lacks sufficient query diversity to learn robust selectivity, or when the compressor discards evidence needed for unanticipated query patterns. 1 independent implementation, 129 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Experience-Handoff Reinforcement Learning for Recursive Self-Improvement
item.description: The method replaces scalar-reward RL that discards trial traces, and replaces hand-crafted reflection/playbook scaffolds, by learning the action, reflection, and curation roles jointly under a fixed harness, evaluating artifacts by their downstream effect on future rollouts. It costs full RL training over a multi-role LLM pipeline: environment rollouts, reward infrastructure, and training capacity that exceed a single 24 GB GPU or API-only budget. It can fail through reward hacking of downstream effect evaluation, playbook drift where learned artifacts encode spurious patterns, and non-transfer of the trained scaffold behaviors to tasks outside the benchmark distribution. 1 independent implementation, 5 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Small Language Models for Inference-Capability Routing: Effects of Model Capacity and Prompt Optimization on Downstream Quality and Efficiency
item.description: It replaces indiscriminate activation of reasoning, RAG, web search, and calculator capabilities on every query with a small Qwen2.5 router (1.5B-14B) making four independent routing decisions via prompt optimization. The cost is router inference overhead, which grows with router capacity and was measured in a separate environment, plus the effort of capability-specific prompt tuning and maintaining labeled routing data. Failures are capability-dependent: false-positive activations waste compute without quality loss, while false negatives on RAG and web search degrade answer quality, and similar classification F1 scores can hide these divergent downstream effects. 1 independent implementation, 129 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: test.

item.title: SoScale: Second-Order Scale Search for FP4 Quantization
item.description: SoScale replaces default maximum-absolute-value scaling and element-wise reconstruction error minimization for FP4 quantization scale selection. It requires computing Hessian information and performing GPTQ-style error recovery during the search, increasing offline quantization time and implementation complexity compared to standard calibration. The method depends on calibration data representativeness; if the Hessian approximation is poor or the calibration distribution mismatches production traffic, the selected scales may fail to preserve accuracy on actual inputs. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: test.

item.title: daVinci-Prover: Agent-Native Mid-Training for Formal Theorem Proving
item.description: The method replaces direct supervised fine-tuning on theorem-proving data with a 33.7B-token agent-native mid-training phase plus roughly 36K verifier-grounded agent trajectories collected through a custom Lean-interaction harness. It costs multi-billion-token mid-training compute, a formal-verifier sandbox infrastructure, and trajectory-collection effort, none of which fit a single 24 GB GPU or a limited cloud budget. It can fail if the synthesized corpus or trajectories are not released, and its gains are demonstrated only for Lean theorem proving, with no evidence of transfer to general production workloads. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Contain, Conform, Compare (Extended Version): A Red-Teamed Evaluation Kit for Small Coding Agents and the Full Record of Its Experiments
item.description: The kit replaces reliance on a single noisy hosted competition score and ad-hoc local testing with a local evaluator that sandboxes agent-written code in network-isolated containers, verifies conformance with the hosted scorer's prompts down to rendered tokens, and applies paired statistics that respect repository clustering. It costs container-orchestration infrastructure, maintenance of conformance checks as the hosted scorer evolves, and the compute to run hundreds of evaluations (about 250 runs per hour for a 4B agent on one high-end GPU), plus engineering effort to integrate one's own agent bundle. It can fail because the paper's own experiments show that screen-passing agent changes did not confirm on new tasks and that 65% of tasks were solved in none of eight baseline runs, so an adopted kit can still mislead if users underpower their comparisons or over-trust single-run gains. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars.
